When a regex fights back.

Explore why a tiny change to a string can turn a simple pattern into a huge amount of work. This demonstration safely simulates backtracking—it never executes a dangerous regex.

01 / Set up the experiment

4816
^(a+)+$

The inner a+ consumes one or more letters. The outer + permits multiple groups. These overlapping choices produce alternative ways to partition the same text.

Why does ! matter?

For a valid string, the engine can accept a successful grouping. An invalid final character forces rejection, so a backtracking engine may explore many different ways to divide the preceding a characters before giving up.

What does the chart count?

For n letters, there are 2n−1 ways to place or omit boundaries between adjacent letters. The chart counts those groupings, not measured milliseconds or an exact number of Java regex engine instructions.

Based on Module 5, slides 27–33 (ReDoS / Evil Regex). Safety: maximum 16 characters; combinatorial counts and sample partitions only. This is a learning model, not a benchmark of a particular regex engine.
